messages.subject: Dirichlet-multinomial GLM
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to code up a Dirichlet-multinomial GLM (and doing maximum
likelihood, not sampling, please don't judge). I have a working
solution by explicitly constructing the likelihood (attached), but
it's a bit of mess, so I would appreciate any pointers on whether I
could have done this a cleaner way.

Is there by any chance hidden Dirichlet-multinomial functionality
somewhere, or would it be straightforward (for me) to implement this?
It would presumably help to start with the existing beta-binomial
functions.

Thanks in advance for any help,

David.

--
David A. Knowles,
Stanford University.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Dirichlet-multinomial GLM
parts:
There are two approaches that would make sense.

1. Actually do the implicit parameterization of the Dirichlet-multinomial
with the latent simplex variables and define theta to be a parameter and
use

paramters {
simplex[K] theta[N];
...
model {
theta[n] ~ dirichlet(alpha);
y[n] ~ multinomial(theta);
...

Simple, but introduces a lot of parameters.


2. Marginalize the theta out as in the beta-binomial. The easiest
way to do this would be to define the dirichlet-multinomial as
a function:

functions {
real dirichlet_multinomial(int[] y, vector alpha) {
return value based on y and alpha
}
}

and then use

y ~ dirichlet_multinomial(alpha);

in the model block.

- Bob

messages.author: 181bcebaf89c73b8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Dirichlet-multinomial GLM
parts:
Thanks Bob. Yup, the code I attached was doing your option 2 (I especially don't want to do option 1 since I'm doing optimization). For easy reference for others the salient part is this: 
 
    vector[K] a;
    real suma;
    vector[K] aPlusY;
    vector[K] lGaPlusY;
    vector[K] lGaA ;
    a <- conc * softmax(beta * x[n]);
    suma <- sum(a);
    aPlusY <- a + y[n];
    for (k in 1:K) {
      lGaPlusY[k] <- lgamma(aPlusY[k]);
      lGaA[k] <- lgamma(a[k]);
    }
    increment_log_prob(lgamma(suma)+sum(lGaPlusY)-lgamma(suma+sum(y[n]))-sum(lGaA));

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Dirichlet-multinomial GLM
parts:
That's a good example to use to give people
a taste of what we've been talking over for the
future syntax of Stan, which will involve

1. vectorizing all of our functions,

2. allowing compound declare and define statements, and

3. adding a syntax for piping single terms or collections of
terms to the log density accumulator.

Then that program below would look like this:

vector[K] a <- conc * softmax(beta * x[n]);
real suma <- sum(a);
ld<< lgamma(suma),
lgamma(a + y[n]),
-lgamma(suma + sum(y[n])),
-lgamma(a);

Stay tuned.

- Bob
